phases.label: Morning
phases.title: Two camps, six kilometres apart
phases.text: Frederick's army of about 22,000 is camped between Bedra and Rossbach, facing west. Across the valley, about 41,000 French and Imperial (Reichsarmee) troops under the Prince de Soubise and the Prince of Saxe-Hildburghausen hold the heights toward Mücheln. The allied commanders decide to march around the Prussian left and get between Frederick and the Saale crossings at Merseburg and Weissenfels.
tactic: Turning movement
Marching around an enemy's flank to threaten his supply lines and line of retreat. It needs speed and good scouting, and the allies had neither.
events: Frederick's headquarters in the Rossbach manor

phases.label: Allies march
phases.title: The allied army sets off south
phases.text: Around noon the allied columns begin a long, slow march south toward Zeuchfeld, cavalry in the lead. St Germain stays behind on the heights with about 8,000 men to hold the Prussians' attention. Frederick, watching from the roof of the Rossbach manor, at first takes the movement for a retreat toward Freyburg and lets his men eat their midday meal.
tactic: March column vs. line
Troops in column move fast along roads but can barely fire. To fight, a column must first deploy into a firing line, which takes time. A column caught before it deploys is very vulnerable.
events: St Germain stays to pin the Prussians

phases.label: Prussians move
phases.title: Frederick strikes camp
phases.text: By mid-afternoon it is clear the allies are swinging east past Pettstädt to get round his left. Frederick orders the camp struck; tents come down within minutes. The army marches east behind the Janus and Polzen hills, out of sight of the allies. All 38 squadrons of cavalry go ahead under Friedrich Wilhelm von Seydlitz, the army's youngest general. Seeing the tents fall, the allies conclude the Prussians are retreating and hurry on.
tactic: Using dead ground
Hills hide movement behind them. The Prussians moved along the far side of the ridge, so the allies could not see where they were going.
events: Allies hurry to cut off a 'retreat'

phases.label: Guns open
phases.title: Moller's battery opens fire
phases.text: Colonel Moller hauls 18 heavy guns to the top of the Janus Hill and opens fire on the allied cavalry and the heads of the infantry columns. Behind the Polzen Hill, Seydlitz forms his squadrons in two lines, still out of sight.
tactic: Heavy guns on high ground
Prussian 12-pounders (nicknamed 'Brummer', growlers) could reach well over a kilometre. Firing down onto troops packed in columns did heavy damage.
events: Seydlitz forms behind the Polzen Hill

phases.label: Seydlitz charges
phases.title: Seydlitz's charge
phases.text: Seydlitz brings his squadrons over the Polzen Hill and charges, in close order at full gallop, into the allied cavalry while it is still strung out in march column. The Austrian cuirassiers turn and fight, and French squadrons counter-attack, but within half an hour the whole allied cavalry is broken and fleeing south.
tactic: Shock cavalry
Heavy cavalry charging knee-to-knee at the gallop hits like a wall. Seydlitz trained his men to keep formation at speed, which few cavalry of the time could do.

phases.label: Cavalry routed
phases.title: The allied cavalry breaks
phases.text: The allied horse streams away south past Reichardtswerben. Instead of chasing it off the field, Seydlitz rallies his squadrons in the hollow near Tagewerben. On the ridge, the Prussian infantry has finished forming and starts down the slope. The allied infantry columns, still marching, crowd into one another.
tactic: Rally and re-form
Horses and riders are blown after a charge, and scattered cavalry is useless. Rallying quickly meant Seydlitz had a formed force ready to strike again.

phases.label: Infantry fight
phases.title: The Prussian infantry advances in echelon
phases.text: The Prussian first line comes down from the Janus Hill in echelon, left wing first, and takes up position across the allied line of march. Only about seven battalions get into action. The leading French regiments try to deploy, and some attempt a bayonet charge while still in column, but they are met by steady platoon volleys and Moller's guns. The firefight lasts barely a quarter of an hour.
tactic: Echelon and platoon fire

In an echelon each battalion is set slightly back from the one beside it, so the line meets the enemy one unit at a time from the strong end. Prussian battalions fired by platoons in a rolling sequence, keeping up continuous fire.
events: French column heads try to deploy

phases.label: Second charge
phases.title: Seydlitz strikes the infantry
phases.text: With the allied infantry pinned by fire from the front, Seydlitz charges again from the Tagewerben hollow into its right flank and rear. Regiments jammed in column cannot turn to face him. The allied army begins to come apart.
tactic: Combined arms
Infantry holds the enemy in place with fire from the front while cavalry hits the flank. Neither arm alone would have broken the allied army so quickly.

phases.label: Rout
phases.title: The allied army dissolves
phases.text: The allied infantry breaks and flees south-west toward Pettstädt, Storkau and Obschütz, abandoning guns and baggage. The Prussians follow, but the November sun is setting. St Germain finally marches south from the heights to try to cover the retreat.
tactic: Pursuit
A beaten army is most vulnerable in flight. Darkness at about half past four on a November afternoon is what saved most of the allied army.

phases.label: Nightfall
phases.title: St Germain and Loudon cover the withdrawal
phases.text: St Germain's corps and Loudon's Croats form a rearguard just north-east of Pettstädt as darkness falls, and the wreck of the allied army streams away toward Freyburg and the Unstrut. The battle has lasted about ninety minutes. Prussian losses are roughly 550; the allies have lost about 10,000, about half of them prisoners, along with most of their artillery.
tactic: Rearguard
Fresh, formed troops at the rear slow a pursuer and let a beaten army escape. Here they mattered less than the coming of night.

units.name: Grenadier battalions
units.note: Massed grenadier companies, the army's shock infantry. Led the echelon on the left.

units.name: Garde & Itzenplitz
units.note: Frederick's own Foot Guards plus a line regiment.

units.name: Goltz & Hülsen
units.note: Right wing; arrived last and saw little fighting.

units.name: Second line (left)
units.note: Reserve line. Most of these battalions never fired a shot.

units.name: Second line (centre)
units.note: Reserve line. Most of these battalions never fired a shot.

units.name: Second line (right)
units.note: Reserve line. Most of these battalions never fired a shot.

units.name: Moller's battery
units.note: Colonel Karl Friedrich von Moller dragged the army's heavy guns onto the Janus Hill and fired over the heads of the Prussian infantry.

units.name: Garde du Corps & Gendarmes
units.note: Elite heavy horse; first line of the charge.

units.name: Leib & Seydlitz Cuirassiers
units.note: Armoured breastplates, big horses, straight swords.

units.name: Czettritz & Meinicke Dragoons
units.note: Second line of the charge.

units.name: Driesen Cuirassiers
units.note: Second line.

units.name: Szekely Hussars
units.note: Light horse for scouting and pursuit.

units.name: Frei-Bataillon Mayr
units.note: A 'free battalion' of irregular light infantry left behind to watch St Germain.

units.name: Piémont & Mailly
units.note: Head of the right column. Tried a bayonet attack in column and was shot down.

units.name: St-Chamond & La Marck
units.note: La Marck was a German regiment in French service.

units.name: Blau-Würzburg
units.note: Contingents from the small states of the Holy Roman Empire, often poorly trained.

units.name: Allied reserve artillery
units.note: Most of these guns were abandoned in the rout.

units.name: Austrian cuirassiers
units.note: The best horsemen in the allied army; they met Seydlitz head-on and broke last.

units.name: Reichsarmee & French horse
units.strength: La Reine, Bourbon, Rougrave & Imperial cavalry · 20 sqns

units.name: St Germain's corps
units.note: Left on the heights to pin the Prussians. Covered the retreat at the end of the day.

units.name: Loudon's Croats
units.note: Croatian Grenzer light infantry, skirmishers who fought in open order.

hq.name: Frederick II
hq.note: Watched the allied march from the roof of the Rossbach manor house.

hq.name: Soubise & Hildburghausen
hq.note: The two allied commanders shared command and disagreed throughout.
